messages:
anya: ran a quick replay-harness sweep this morning combining kernel switch + delay-cap tuning. saw a surprising p95 regression for multi-tenant replay (shared pool) and a simultaneous spike in KV cache miss rate :confused:
anya: TL;DR numbers from 30m run: median latency ~unchanged, p95 +18%, p99 +26%, kv_cache_miss_rate from 3.1% -> 11.7% on tenant-mix A. throughput steady.
anya: config used: `kernel=int8-optimized-v2`, `batch_size_cap=64`, `max_delay_ms=10`, replay=tenant-mix-A (50/30/20 small/med/large).
anya: replay command we used: `./replay_harness --profile tenant-mix-A --kernel int8-optimized-v2 --delay-ms 10 --cap 64 --run-id 1815-delaycap`
mike: can you paste the exact kernel tag and the model variant? int8-optimized-v2 ok, but which quant profile (symmetric/asymmetric)?
anya: quant profile = symmetric-perchannel, kernel commit = `a2f9b4f` (runtime-kernel repo). model variant = gpt-small-pp8-fp16->quantized path used by kernel.
taylor: do you have a flame/ops breakdown? suspect KV cache eviction pattern changed when kernel switched; could be layout/stride change causing more copies/memmove.
anya: quick profile (sampled GPU/host time percentages):
```
kv_cache_lookup: 42%
attention_kernel: 28%
memcpy_h2d/d2h: 12%
kernel_dispatch_overhead: 8%
other: 10%
```
anya: flame shows longer memcpy spikes aligned with bursts of small requests. KV hit ratio drops during those spikes.
lee: that smells like the new kernel is touching KV buffers differently (padding/stride). Two quick mitigations: bump max_delay_ms to let batches fill (reduces small-batch mem pressure), or per-tenant soft batch caps so small tenants don't thrash the pool.
anya: tried bumping `max_delay_ms` to 20ms in a 15m run: p95 improved from +18% -> +6%, kv miss down to 5.4%, median up ~4ms. so tradeoff exists.
perf-bot: CI perf/regression job 1815-delaycap finished: baseline->candidate: p95 +6.2%, p99 +11.3%, throughput -0.4%. See job: https://ci.internal/jobs/1815-delaycap
sophia: can we instrument per-tenant KV hit/miss in the replay harness? need to know whether a small tenant is causing global evictions. also run kernel A vs B in apple-to-apple mode (same queued arrival stream) to isolate scheduling differences.
mike: also check whether kernel changed KV cache version format (header bytes) — that would cause logical misses. taylor, can you grep kernel commit for kv layout changes?
taylor: on it. if layout changed we need a migration or compatibility path. if not, it's likely memory access pattern. i'll add counters to the harness: `kv_hits`, `kv_misses`, `evictions` per-tenant and per-second.
anya: i'm going to run three back-to-back jobs: (1) fp16-default with delay=10, (2) int8-v2 with delay=10, (3) int8-v2 with delay=20. same replay file and seeds. will paste results here when done.
lee: for fairness tests, also include a run with `per_tenant_batch_cap=16` and one with `no_shared_pool` (dedicated instance) to compare. that will tell whether the issue is inter-tenant eviction or kernel behavior.
sophia: quick note: when you compare, ensure metrics are apples-to-apples: same GPU model, same load generator client concurrency, same seed, same warmup period. record warmup separately.
anya: agreed. planning 30m runs with 5m warmup. running now (job id 1815-A/B/C).
mike: if numbers persist we'll probably revert shared pool kernel to fp16-default until we understand KV behavior. keep me posted. :+1:
taylor: i'll push the KV counters to the harness repo in a branch `t/kv-counters-1815` and schedule a sweep for later today.
anya: update 45m in: first two runs done. summary: (1) fp16-default/delay10 -> p95 baseline, kv_miss=3.0%; (2) int8-v2/delay10 -> p95 +17%, kv_miss=12%; (3) int8-v2/delay20 -> p95 +5%, kv_miss=4.8%. detailed logs + perf traces in GCS `gs://perf/1815-delaycap/`.
lee: interesting — increasing delay recovers KV hit and p95 but increases median. suggests batching tradeoff is primary lever. for multi-tenant fairness we should try dynamic per-tenant delay: small tenants can use slightly longer delay to avoid evict storms.
sophia: can the scheduler implement tenant-aware delay heuristics? e.g., if tenant qps < threshold, bump delay by +X ms. worth prototyping in harness first.
mike: good plan. if anyone wants prod rollback rights, ping infra. otherwise we'll keep int8 in dedicated pools and revert shared pools for now.
anya: thanks all — collecting traces and will open a short RFC with proposed mitigations (per-tenant caps, adaptive delay, kernel compatibility check). tagging @here for visibility. :thinking:
